# Decisions: Nexus Code v1.0.0

This file records only consequential decisions that were unresolved when the audit finished. On 2026-10-14 the owner authorized applying the recommended option for every outstanding decision. ("You are authorized to apply your recommendations for the best decisions for the project on any outstanding decisions in the plans/specs.") Each entry is therefore marked **RESOLVED (delegated)**. The options, tradeoffs and affected requirements are kept so the owner can reverse any decision later. A reversal would change the linked specs, plans and gates.

Some decisions cannot be carried out by an implementer alone. They need an external action, and those actions are listed in the last section. The audit did not perform any of them.

| ID | Decision | Resolution | Blocks execution? |
|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-01](#dec-01-default-execution-posture) | Default execution posture | Review by default; auto only in trusted workspaces | No (resolved) |
| [DEC-02](#dec-02-role-of-the-repl) | Role of the REPL | Supported secondary surface; TUI primary; top-level flags implemented | No |
| [DEC-03](#dec-03-team-and-operation-scope-in-v1) | `/team` and `nexus operation` in v1 | Shipped as **experimental**; data-loss fix still a blocker | No |
| [DEC-04](#dec-04-issue-12-open-normative-blockers) | Issue #12 open blockers | EXT-004 implemented; CTX-001 partially implemented; CTX-002 descoped post-v1 | No |
| [DEC-05](#dec-05-v1-evaluation-protocol-and-thresholds) | Evaluation protocol and thresholds | 40 held-out T2 tasks, 5 runs, 2 peers, thresholds below | Needs an external author (see actions) |
| [DEC-06](#dec-06-supported-providers-for-v1) | Supported providers | Local OpenAI-compatible + OpenRouter supported; others experimental until live-verified | No |
| [DEC-07](#dec-07-experimental-surfaces-nexus-eval-tdd-team-roles) | `nexus eval`, `/tdd`, team roles | eval and tdd experimental; eval's workspace mutation fixed; role tool sets enforced | No |
| [DEC-08](#dec-08-version-identity-and-stale-v1x-tags) | Version identity, stale v1.x tags | `package.json` is the source of truth; local v1.x tags deleted (owner action) | No |
| [DEC-09](#dec-09-release-provenance-mechanism) | Release provenance | GitHub artifact attestations | No |
| [DEC-10](#dec-10-tracking-of-clidist) | Tracking of `cli/dist` | Untrack | No |
| [DEC-11](#dec-11-retention-defaults) | Retention defaults | 90 days / 2 GB; audit log 10 MB × 5; first GC needs acknowledgement | No |
| [DEC-12](#dec-12-platform-scope) | Platform scope | Linux x86-64 glibc only for v1.0.0 | No |
| [DEC-13](#dec-13-contest-track-disposition) | Contest track | Separate track; docs and CI fix immediately; submission states operator-host only | Owner confirms deadline status |
| [DEC-14](#dec-14-free-text-on-the-command-line) | Free text on the command line | Explicit `nexus run` required | No |
| [DEC-15](#dec-15-knowledge-auto-extraction) | Knowledge auto-extraction | Off by default, opt-in | No |

---

## DEC-01: Default execution posture

**Question.** What protects the user by default from model-initiated command execution and network egress? See SEC-01, VER-01, HIST-05 and TUI-07.

| Option | Description | Tradeoffs |
|---|---|---|
| A | Review by default: write, exec and egress ask | Safest. More prompts. Changes existing users' habits. |
| B | Auto with an enforced sandbox by default | Few prompts. bwrap is unavailable on some hosts (WSL, rootless containers), and the Docker fallback is unpinned and networked. Egress is unsolved. |
| **C (chosen)** | Posture follows workspace trust. **Untrusted workspace → review** for `write_workspace`, `exec`, `egress` and `context_inject`. **Trusted workspace → auto** for `write_workspace` and `exec`; `egress` asks once per origin per session. `--yes` or `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` force auto. `--sandbox` stays available. | Safe for cloned or unknown repos. Low friction on the operator's own repos after one `nexus trust .`. Reuses the existing trust store, so there is no new concept. |
| D | Keep auto | Contradicts REQ-SEC-101; rejected. |

**Rationale.** The threat that matters is content from an untrusted repository or the web. Trust is the existing per-workspace boundary that MCP and plugins already honour. Option C closes SEC-01 and VER-01 on exactly the inputs that cause them, and keeps the daily-driver experience on trusted repos.

**Further rules:**
- Headless `nexus run` with no TTY: decision-required calls are DENIED with a typed reason unless `--yes` is given.
- The eval and demo runners pass `--yes` explicitly.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-SEC-101, 102 and 119; REQ-TUI-102; SPEC-01; PLAN-01; ACC-SAFE-01.

## DEC-02: Role of the REPL

**Options.** (A) Remove the REPL. **(B, chosen)** The REPL is a supported secondary surface: used for non-TTY input, scripting and fallback, with its approvals fixed to the TUI's standard. (C) The REPL stays the default.

**Rationale.** The REPL is the only interactive surface when stdin or stdout is not a terminal, and when the Rust TUI is missing. Removing it loses a fallback. Keeping it as the default contradicts UI-004.

**Also decided.** The top-level flags `--approve`, `-r/--resume [id]`, `--repl` and `--live` are **implemented** rather than removed from the docs, because USER_MANUAL already teaches them.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-REL-101, REQ-REL-102, REQ-SEC-103.

## DEC-03: Team and operation scope in v1

**Options.** (A) Fully supported. **(B, chosen)** Shipped and labelled **experimental** in help and docs. Excluded from the qualification task-quality claims. But the following are still fixed for v1:
- **AGT-02a** (compaction originals lost on resume): BLOCKER, because it silently loses durable state behind a documented guarantee.
- **AGT-02b–d and AGT-11**: RELEASE-REQUIRED.

(C) Remove the commands.

**Rationale.** Evidence for multi-unit convergence is thin. EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE lists I3, I4 and a stale-lock race as open, and post-remediation dogfooding was INTEGRATION_BLOCKED. Removing the commands throws away working code. Silent data loss is not acceptable even in experimental features.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-AGT-102, 103, 107; SPEC-04.

## DEC-04: Issue #12 open normative blockers

| Item | Resolution | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EXT-004 (middleware before/after audit) | **Implement** (SPEC-03 §3.5) | Small change. Plugins can rewrite tool I/O silently today. |
| CTX-001 (per-item provenance for injected context) | **Partially implement**: skills, knowledge and other injected context carry source path and trust state (SPEC-03 §3.4). The full provenance graph is post-v1. | The risky injected sources are covered. A full implementation is a large redesign with low marginal safety benefit once trust gating exists. |
| CTX-002 (freshness and version applicability of knowledge) | **Descoped to post-v1**, with this written rationale: auto-extraction is off by default (DEC-15) and knowledge is trust-gated, so stale knowledge can only come from the operator's own explicit saves. | Accepted risk, recorded. |
| UI-006/007, DEDUP-003, "no Git remote", SUBP-004/005 deferrals | **Recorded as superseded** in REQUIREMENTS §2 (Ratatui adopted; on-demand tool groups; public GitHub). SUBP-004 and SUBP-005 are replaced by SPEC-02. | Governance hygiene (HIST-11). |

## DEC-05: v1 evaluation protocol and thresholds

**Chosen protocol (SPEC-10):**
- 40 held-out T2 tasks, at least 20 from external repositories at pinned commits, across JS/TS, Python, Rust and Go, with at least 6 per class (bugfix, feature, refactor, debug).
- 5 runs per task and configuration.
- Peers: Goose and OpenCode, on the same model and budgets.
- 8 T4 fault classes × 5 runs.
- 8 T3 long tasks × 5 runs.

**Thresholds, all must hold:**

| Metric | Threshold |
|---|---|
| False VERIFIED | **0** (hard) |
| Held-out T2 pooled hidden-test correctness | **≥ 60% absolute** and **≥ (best matched peer − 10 points)** |
| Correctness per task class | ≥ 40% |
| Crash rate | ≤ 2% |
| Regression rate | ≤ 5% |
| T4 outcome truthfulness | 100% |
| T4 hangs beyond budget + 5 min | 0 |
| T3 false-absence | 0 |
| T3 steering honoured | ≥ 95% |
| `run`-mode operator interventions | 0 |

**Task authorship.** The held-out half must be authored without access to Nexus's development set and tuning history. The first preference is a person other than the implementer. If none is available, use a separately-run agent session given only this task schema and the external repositories, with no Nexus source access. Its sha256 manifest is committed before the RC freeze. That fallback is weaker independence and must be stated in the qualification report.

**Rationale.** These figures are the pilot's pre-registered thresholds (eval/README), tightened where the pilot showed weakness: false VERIFIED, crash accounting. The absolute floor prevents "beat a weak peer" from passing. Thresholds are fixed **before** the RC run.

## DEC-06: Supported providers for v1

| Tier | Providers | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| **Supported** | OpenAI-compatible local servers (llama.cpp server, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama) | The release notes name the server kinds that pass the standalone matrix (≥ 2 required). Others are listed as "compatible, not qualified". |
| **Supported (optional integration)** | homelab-ai gateway | Never required (standalone gate). |
| **Supported** | OpenRouter | Already live-verified historically; re-verify at RC. |
| **Experimental → Supported if live-verified at RC** | OpenAI (Responses), Anthropic (Messages), generic compatible cloud | `nexus providers verify` live PASS archived at RC; otherwise they stay experimental. |
| **Experimental (always)** | ChatGPT sign-in, Copilot sign-in | They use unofficial OAuth flows with terms-of-service and stability risk. Opt-in with a visible warning. |

## DEC-07: Experimental surfaces (`nexus eval`, `/tdd`, team roles)

- **`nexus eval`.** Labelled experimental. Its scoring is not fixed in v1, but its unsafe `git checkout` in the operator's workspace **is** fixed: it must run in a worktree (VER-07a). It is excluded from all claims. The SPEC-10 harness (`eval/`) is the qualification tool.
- **`/tdd` / `--tdd`.** Labelled experimental. Fixing the phase enforcement is post-v1.
- **Team roles.** Reviewer and researcher units run with a **read-only tool set** (cheap and safety-relevant). Other role allowlists are post-v1.

## DEC-08: Version identity and stale v1.x tags

- `package.json` is the single source of truth. `scripts/sync-version.mjs` updates `cli/package.json` and `core/Cargo.toml`. Release CI asserts that all three equal the tag.
- Release line: `v1.0.0-rc.N` prereleases, then `v1.0.0`.
- The local-only tags `v1.1.0`, `v1.2.0` and `v1.2.1` are to be **deleted locally**: `git tag -d v1.1.0 v1.2.0 v1.2.1`. They are not on origin and are not ancestors of main. They sort above v1.0.0 and would confuse `git describe` and the tooling. This is an owner action (see the last section) because it removes local references.

## DEC-09: Release provenance mechanism

**Chosen:** GitHub artifact attestations (`actions/attest-build-provenance`). Users verify with `gh attestation verify`. SHA256SUMS is kept. There is no separate GPG or minisign key to manage.

**Tradeoff:** verification needs the `gh` CLI or the Sigstore tooling. The installer verifies only when `gh` is present, and checksums are always verified.

## DEC-10: Tracking of `cli/dist`

**Chosen:** stop tracking `cli/dist`. Remove it from git, add it to `.gitignore`, and build it in CI and packaging. Checkout users already need `make build` for the Rust binaries.

**Tradeoff:** a fresh clone needs one build step for the TS side too; the docs already state `make build`.

## DEC-11: Retention defaults

**Chosen:**
- Keep tasks, sessions, checkpoints and flights for 90 days or up to 2 GB in total, whichever limit is hit first. Never remove the current session or pinned sessions.
- Rotate `audit.log` at 10 MB, keeping 5 files.
- Automatic GC runs at most daily. The first run after upgrade needs acknowledgement, or `NEXUS_GC=auto`.

## DEC-12: Platform scope

**Chosen:** Linux x86-64, glibc ≥ 2.35, Node ≥ 20 for v1.0.0, which is what is built and tested. The docs keep the conservative "≥ 2.35" claim; the binaries reference glibc symbols ≤ 2.34. macOS, arm64 and musl are post-v1 roadmap items.

## DEC-13: Contest track disposition

**Chosen:**
- The contest is a separate track (SPEC-C1) and never gates the client.
- The CON-001 documentation and CI correction is made immediately, because it currently misdirects judges to an unauthenticated legacy Worker.
- Until CON-102–106 are delivered and a clean-account run exists, all contest material states "reproduced on the operator host only".

**Owner check needed:** whether the contest deadline (2026-10-14) still admits repository changes. If it does not, the corrections land after the contest, marked post-submission.

## DEC-14: Free text on the command line

**Chosen:** an unknown first word is an error. Free text runs only through `nexus run "<text>"` or the interactive prompt. This removes REL-03's accidental agent launches.

## DEC-15: Knowledge auto-extraction

**Chosen:** off by default; opt-in with `NEXUS_KNOWLEDGE_AUTOEXTRACT=1`, with a visible notice each time a rule is saved. Workspace knowledge is loaded only when the workspace is trusted.

---

## Owner and external actions required (not performed by the audit)

| # | Action | Why | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `git tag -d v1.1.0 v1.2.0 v1.2.1` in `~/nexus-code` | DEC-08 | M0 |
| X2 | Provide an independent author for the held-out T2 tasks, or approve the agent-author fallback | DEC-05 | Before M5 |
| X3 | Provide a host or VM for standalone servers (llama.cpp, vLLM or LM Studio, Ollama) separate from the homelab gateway config | REQ-PRV-106 | M5 |
| X4 | Provide cloud API keys for live `providers verify` (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter) and accept the small spend | DEC-06 | M5 |
| X5 | Independent reviewer for continuity/compaction acceptance and RC acceptance | REQ-AGT-110, ACCEPTANCE §8 | M5/M6 |
| X6 | Confirm the contest deadline status; provide a clean Cloudflare account and VM for CON-106 | DEC-13 | Contest track |
| X7 | Approve publishing `v1.0.0-rc.N` and `v1.0.0` (tag push triggers public release) | Release | M6 |
| X8 | Decide whether to clean the 52k test-polluted records in the real `~/.nexus/tasks` (PER-03). Safe to remove: `task-*.json` whose `workspacePath` starts with `/tmp/nexus-app-test-`. | Hygiene | Any time |

# PLAN-01: Safe execution defaults and approval integrity

Implements [SPEC-01](../specs/SPEC-01-safe-execution-defaults.md). Milestone **M1**. Requirements: REQ-SEC-101, 102, 103, 104, 108, 109 and 119; REQ-TUI-102. Decision: DEC-01 option C.

## Preconditions

- PLAN-08 task 1 (test HOME isolation) is merged. Without it, the test changes below write into the real `~/.nexus`.
- Work in a branch or worktree off `main`. Run long suites on a snapshot copy (tasks/lessons.md, 2026-10-13).

## Safe change boundary

These files are in scope:

- `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts`
- `cli/src/core/tool_groups.ts`
- `cli/src/agent.ts` (dispatch gate ~3936-3975; verifier call sites 1602-1630, 3432-3436, 4034, 4067-4090)
- `cli/src/repl.ts`
- `cli/src/sidecar.ts`
- `cli/src/index.ts`
- `cli/src/config.ts`
- `cli/src/types.ts`
- `cli/src/security.ts`
- `cli/src/sandbox.ts`
- `cli/src/core/authority.ts`
- `cli/src/tester.ts` (runner routing only)
- `cli/src/slash/workspace_commands.ts`
- `core/src/runner.rs` (tripwire only)
- `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{protocol.rs,live_view.rs,live_state.rs}` (posture banner, arrow direction, narrow hints)
- `eval/run.mjs`
- `demo/lib/real-agent-runner.mjs` (`--yes`)

Do not touch the parser, which belongs to PLAN-11, or the runner process registry, which belongs to PLAN-02.

## Tasks (ordered)

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `EffectClass` type and `effect` field. Classify every built-in capability per SPEC-01 §5.1. MCP and plugin registration defaults to `exec`. Registry validation throws on a missing class. | `core/capabilities.ts:22-45` + each declaration; `mcp.ts` (registration); `plugins.ts` (custom tools) | — |
| 2 | Add `ApprovalPolicy`: `requiresDecision(effect, {mode, trusted, sandbox, egressOrigins})`. Unit test it with the full matrix. | new `cli/src/core/approval_policy.ts` | 1 |
| 3 | Replace `onConfirm && isMutating` with the policy. If no handler is available and a decision is required, return DENIED with reason `DECISION_REQUIRED_NO_OPERATOR`. Egress per-origin memory lives on the agent and is cleared on `/mode` change and on resume. | `agent.ts:3945-3975`; subagent dispatch `agent.ts:5384` | 2 |
| 4 | Replace the `autoApprove` booleans with `HarnessConfig.approvalMode`. Default resolution per DEC-01 C: `--yes`/`NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE` → explicit, else trusted → auto, else review. CLI flags: `--approve`, `--yes`, `--read-only`, `--mode <m>`. | `config.ts:107`, `types.ts`, `index.ts:93,115`, `repl.ts:69,281,644-648`, `sidecar.ts:53,66,478,638,935` | 3 |
| 5 | Route verifier executions through the policy as `exec`. When not trusted and no prior approval exists, emit the approval with `kind: "verifier"`, the command, and the resolved script body (read `package.json` `scripts.test`, the Makefile `test:` recipe, `Cargo.toml`/`pytest.ini` presence). Cache the approval per (workspace, command, script digest) for the session. | `agent.ts:1602-1630,3432-3436,4034`; `tester.ts:113-136` (add `describeVerifier()`); `approval_review.ts` (new kind) | 3 |
| 6 | `/test` and `nexus eval` use the bridge runner instead of `execSync`. | `tester.ts:143-163`; `repl.ts:1357`; `slash/workspace_commands.ts:160`; `evaluator.ts` | 5 |
| 7 | REPL approval hardening: clear the line buffer, 400 ms grace, `[y/N/d/a]` with empty input = No, confirm for `a`. | `repl.ts:270-276,353,385,497-501` | 4 |
| 8 | Update eval and demo runners to pass `--yes`. Update test fixtures that assumed auto: grep `new InteractiveRepl(`, `SidecarServer(` and `mode:` in `cli/test`. | `eval/run.mjs`, `demo/lib/real-agent-runner.mjs`, `cli/test/**` | 4 |
| 9 | Read-only HOME masking: bwrap `--tmpfs $HOME --ro-bind <ws> <ws>`. Without bwrap, path-confine the allowlisted commands (reject `~`, `$`, absolute paths, and `..` that escapes). | `sandbox.ts:131-181`; `core/authority.ts:44-136` | — |
| 10 | Build the sandbox argv as an array; spawn without a shell. | `sandbox.ts:131-158,181`; caller in `tools.ts` | 9 |
| 11 | Tripwire: shell-words tokenization in TS and Rust; fix false positives; rename in UI and docs; tests for false positives plus documented bypasses. | `security.ts:12-23,78-89`; `runner.rs:64-107` | — |
| 12 | Posture banner: add `posture` to the sidecar `session.state`; render the TUI header line; add a REPL banner line; add `posture` to doctor JSON. | `sidecar.ts`; `protocol.rs`; `live_view.rs` header; `repl.ts` banner; `doctor.ts` | 4 |
| 13 | Approval panel polish: make arrow keys match the button layout; add short-form hints under 60 columns. | `live_state.rs:1329-1335`; `live_view.rs:540-542` | — |
| 14 | Docs: USER_MANUAL approvals/modes, quickstart "review requested actions", ARCHITECTURE §3 controls-and-limits, release notes entry. | docs | 1-13 |

## PR slices

1. **PR-1a** (tasks 1-3): effect classes, policy and gate, with the matrix test. No behaviour change yet: the default is still auto via a temporary constant.
2. **PR-1b** (tasks 4, 8, 12): posture resolution, the DEC-01 C default, fixture updates, banner. This is the behaviour change.
3. **PR-1c** (tasks 5-6): verifier gating and runner routing.
4. **PR-1d** (task 7): REPL approval hardening, with PTY tests.
5. **PR-1e** (tasks 9-11): read-only masking, argv sandbox, tripwire.
6. **PR-1f** (tasks 13-14): TUI polish and docs.

## Tests and fixtures

- **Unit:**
  - `approval_policy.test.ts`: registry × mode × trust matrix; fails on an unclassified capability.
  - `security.test.ts`: tripwire false positives and documented bypasses.
- **Integration:**
  - `verifier_gating.test.ts`: untrusted fixture with a sentinel `scripts.test`, covering ACC-SAFE-09.
  - `readonly_home.test.ts`: fixture HOME with `.ssh/id_rsa`, covering ACC-SAFE-04.
  - `sandbox_quoting.test.ts`, covering ACC-SAFE-05.
- **PTY:**
  - Port `evidence/D_pty/r1_repl.py` and `r1d.py` into `cli/test/repl_approval_e2e.test.ts`, using the existing PTY helper in `cli/test/helpers/fixtures.ts`. Covers ACC-SAFE-03.
  - Add a startup-banner assertion to `tui_surface_e2e`. Covers ACC-SAFE-06.
  - Keep `tui_approval_input_e2e` green (ACC-SAFE-08).
- **Live (M5):** one standalone session per server kind verifies the banner and the first-verifier approval.

## Documentation and packaging

- Add a release-notes entry for the default change and for `--yes` in scripts and CI.
- The quickstart gains a "Trust your own repository" step: `nexus trust .`.

## Rollback

- Each PR reverts independently.
- PR-1b is the only behaviour flip. Reverting it restores the auto default while keeping the classes and gate.
- The `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` escape hatch remains for users after release.

## Definition of done

- ACC-SAFE-01 to ACC-SAFE-10 pass in CI. The PTY tests run in CI (they already run in `linux-x86_64`).
- REQUIREMENTS.md rows REQ-SEC-101/102/103/104/108/109/119 and REQ-TUI-102 show status `tested`, with test references.
- `make test` passes on a clean snapshot.
- The docs checklist items for SPEC-01 are done.

# PLAN-02: Process ownership, cancellation and resource bounds

This plan implements [SPEC-02](../specs/SPEC-02-process-ownership-and-bounds.md) in milestone **M1**. It covers REQ-AGT-109 and 109a, REQ-SEC-106, 107 and 107a, and REQ-TUI-107.

## Safe change boundary

- `core/src/runner.rs`
- `core/src/main.rs` (RPC loop, signals)
- `core/src/file_ops.rs` (read cap)
- `cli/src/tools.ts` (bridge)
- `cli/src/agent.ts` (signal plumbing into `executeTool`; notify/BEL gating at 773-780 and 4932)
- `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs` (cancel feedback)
- `cli/src/sidecar.ts` (shutdown ordering)

The JSON-RPC protocol version bump is shared with PLAN-06, task 3.

## Tasks

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ProcessRegistry` (request_id→pgid, services). Insert after spawn, remove on reap. | `runner.rs:116-167` | — |
| 2 | `cancel` RPC: killpg TERM, then KILL after 2 s, then reply. ESRCH counts as success. | `main.rs:194-203`, `runner.rs` | 1 |
| 3 | Shutdown sweep on stdin EOF, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (`tokio::signal`). `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` at startup (Linux, `nix` or `libc` crate). | `main.rs` | 1 |
| 4 | Bounded capture: head buffer plus tail ring buffer, and a byte counter in the truncation notice. | `runner.rs:177-193` | — |
| 5 | PTY path kills the pgid. | `runner.rs:319-323` | 1 |
| 6 | `read_file` cap at 8 MB, with an `offset`/`length` paging hint in the error. Same for `batch_read`. | `file_ops.rs:205-277`; capability schema in `capabilities.ts` | — |
| 7 | Clamp `timeout_secs` to `NEXUS_MAX_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 1800) and tell the model it was clamped. | `tools.ts` (args), `runner.rs` | — |
| 8 | Bridge: `executeTool(name,args,{signal})`. On abort or timeout, send `cancel` and await the reply (≤ 5 s). On shutdown, close stdin, wait 3 s, then SIGKILL. | `tools.ts:247-256,338-347,432+` | 2,3 |
| 9 | Agent passes the turn signal to every `executeTool`. A killed tool's result is `status: CANCELLED`, `signal`. | `agent.ts` dispatch, spine call | 8 |
| 10 | `run_command {background:true, service_name}` registers a service. Services are listed in `/status`, killed on exit, and do not survive the turn's cancel unless registered. | `capabilities.ts`, `runner.rs`, `slash/session_commands.ts` | 1 |
| 11 | TUI: Esc sets `cancel_requested` and the footer shows "cancelling — waiting for <tool> (<n>s)". | `live_state.rs:1566`, `live_view.rs` footer | — |
| 12 | Gate notify-send and BEL on an interactive TTY and REPL/TUI surface. | `agent.ts:773-780,4932` | — |
| 13 | Docs: USER_MANUAL cancellation section; ARCHITECTURE runner section; residual risk of `setsid` escape without the sandbox. | docs | all |

## PR slices

1. **PR-2a** (tasks 1-5, Rust only). Registry, cancel RPC, shutdown sweep, bounded capture. Rust unit tests in `runner.rs` follow the style of the existing descendant test (`runner.rs:479-500`).
2. **PR-2b** (tasks 8-9). Bridge and agent plumbing, plus the ACC-PROC PTY tests.
3. **PR-2c** (tasks 6, 7, 10). Read cap, timeout clamp, services.
4. **PR-2d** (tasks 11-13). TUI feedback, notification gating, docs.

## Tests

- **Rust:**
  - `cancel_kills_group`
  - `shutdown_on_eof_kills_all`
  - `pdeathsig_sweeps` (spawn harness-core under a parent that exits)
  - `bounded_capture_400mb`, which measures RSS through `/proc/self/status`
- **TS:** a `process_lifecycle_e2e.test.ts` PTY test that ports `evidence/D_pty/s8_cancel_tool.py` and `s9_quit_tool.py`. After each scenario it asserts there are no survivors, using `ps -eo pid,ppid,args` filtered by a unique sleep duration token.
- **Headless:** `nexus run --json` with a PATH shim for `notify-send` that records calls (ACC-PROC-08).
- **Load:** ACC-PROC-07, 30 iterations under `stress`. Runs nightly or in M5; it is not in per-PR CI.

## Rollback

- The registry and sweep are additive.
- If PDEATHSIG causes trouble in containers, it can be disabled with `NEXUS_NO_PDEATHSIG=1`. Keep the env escape hatch.

## Definition of done

- ACC-PROC-01 to ACC-PROC-08 pass.
- Ledger rows updated.
- The ISSUE12 EXEC-009 and SUBP-004/005 historical rows are annotated as superseded by REQ-AGT-109 and REQ-SEC-106 (PLAN-09).

All historical commitments are carried forward in §2. None are silently dropped. Each one is either retained, superseded or descoped, with a written disposition.

**Tested revision for every status below:** `db1ca55` (main, `v0.1.0-alpha.2-2-gdb1ca55`), audited 2026-10-14.

## 1. Legend

### Status ladder

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | Not implemented, or contradicted at HEAD. |
| `partial` | Partly implemented, or implemented with a known defect. |
| `implemented` | Present in source. Not proven by an automated test of this requirement. |
| `tested` | An automated test exercises it and passes at the tested revision (baseline: 905/905 CLI, 266/266 Rust). |
| `visually-accepted` | A human or independent PTY review accepted the rendered behaviour. |
| `product-qualified` | Passed the v1 qualification in ACCEPTANCE.md on the RC. **No requirement holds this status today.** |

Independent acceptance is recorded separately in the "Indep." column: **Y** = an independent review accepted it; **N** = self-assessed only; **—** = not applicable.

### Release classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **B** | BLOCKER. v1.0.0 cannot ship without it. |
| **RR** | Release-required. Must be done for v1.0.0; it is not a safety or workflow blocker on its own, but the release gate checks it. |
| **P** | Post-v1. |
| **K** | Keep: already met; protected by regression tests. |

| Label | Kind of evidence |
|---|---|
| SRC | source inspection |
| TEST | automated test |
| RT | live runtime observation (including PTY) |
| MEAS | measurement |

## 2. Product contract for v1.0.0

### 2.1 Established commitments (sources: README, quickstart, USER_MANUAL, COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY, CLOUD_PROVIDERS, release notes, Issue #12 and later reviews; ledger in REQUIREMENTS §2)

- **Users and workflows.** A single developer or operator runs supervised coding tasks in local repositories on Linux x86-64. The workflows are:
  - the interactive live TUI (primary);
  - the REPL;
  - headless `nexus run` with JSON output and exit codes;
  - resume (`-r`, `/resume`, `run --resume`);
  - `nexus doctor`;
  - workspace trust;
  - providers and connect;
  - checkpoints and undo;
  - MCP client and server;
  - skills and plugins;
  - `/team` and `nexus operation`.
- **Local inference is first class.** Nexus works against any OpenAI-compatible local server (LM Studio, vLLM). The homelab-ai gateway is an optional integration, and Nexus must operate without it.
- **Honest outcomes.** VERIFIED only from a real, bound verifier pass. UNVERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE, BLOCKED and LIMIT_REACHED are distinct.
- **No default step ceiling.** Turns end on completion, cancel, stagnation or failure.
- **Safety promises.**
  - Path jail.
  - Workspace extensions only after `nexus trust`.
  - Secrets tokenized on egress.
  - Credential origin scoping.
  - Cloud destinations only by operator choice.
  - Approvals cannot be decided by stray typing.
- **Distribution.** A one-line non-root installer with SHA-256 verification, version pinning, upgrade and rollback by re-running, manual uninstall that keeps user data, and Linux x86-64 / glibc ≥ 2.35 / Node ≥ 20 only.

### 2.2 Proposed v1.0.0 maturity definition

Nexus v1.0.0 means all of the following:

1. **Safe by default on untrusted input.** Content from a repository, a web page, a skill or a tool output cannot cause unapproved host execution, egress, or configuration changes.
2. **Owns its processes.** Stop means stopped.
3. **Truthful.** No false VERIFIED. Bounded, typed failures.
4. **Continuous.** Resume and compaction never silently lose state.
5. **Standalone.** Qualified live on at least 2 non-gateway local servers.
6. **Shippable.** The installed product equals the tested product, and the documented commands work. One version identity, license notices, SBOM and provenance.
7. **Qualified.** Held-out matched evaluation, plus fault injection, meeting the pre-registered thresholds in DEC-05.

### 2.3 Classification

| Category | Location |
|---|---|
| Blockers, release-required work, post-v1 work | REQUIREMENTS.md §3, §5 |
| Decisions | DECISIONS.md. All resolved under delegated owner authority (2026-10-14). |
| Optional improvements after v1 | REQUIREMENTS §5 |

Each blocker is justified by a workflow, a safety requirement, a compatibility commitment or a reproduced failure (see its "Rationale" and "Finding" columns).

## 3. Architecture as implemented

```
 operator ─┬─► nexus (packaged: node index.js → REPL)          ◄── REL-01: no route to TUI
           └─► harness.sh (checkout) ─► nexus-tui --live (Rust, Ratatui)
                                           │ NDJSON protocol (stdin/stdout)
                                           ▼
                                 node sidecar.js  ──or──  node index.js repl/run
                                           │ (in-process)
                                           ▼
            ApplicationCore / AutonomousAgent.runTurn  (cli/src/agent.ts, 5.4k lines)
              steering drain → capability refresh → admission (compaction ladder, findings,
              token count) → ProviderRecoveryController → streaming inference (client.ts)
              → parse (parser.ts) → dispatch (approval gate) → ExecutionSpine/authority
              → RustCoreBridge (tools.ts) ── JSON-RPC stdio ──► harness-core rpc (Rust)
              → observe/ExecutionTracker → endStep → durable state (~/.nexus/tasks, sessions)
                                                                 │
     inference: OpenAI-compatible (local/gateway) | Responses | Anthropic | OAuth providers
     verifier: tester.ts discoverVerifier → harness-core run_command (repo test script)
     extensions: MCP (stdio/remote), plugins (in-process import), skills (prompt injection)
```

### 3.1 Trust boundaries and their state at HEAD

| Boundary | Intended control | Actual state (finding) |
|---|---|---|
| Model → host shell | Approval or sandbox | Default auto with no sandbox (SEC-01); verifier runs bypass even review mode (VER-01); prose and reasoning JSON executed (VER-02/03) |
| Model → network | Egress classification, approval | Ungated in review mode (HIST-05); SSRF guard is string-based (SEC-03) |
| Workspace → configuration | Only allowlisted project settings | `.env` overrides any env, including TLS (PRV-01) |
| Workspace → prompt | Trust-gated | MCP and plugins are gated; skills and knowledge are not (SEC-05, AGT-10) |
| Destination locality | IP-based | Prefix strings (PRV-02, PRV-08) |
| Operator cancel → processes | Kill the tree | Not propagated; orphans on exit (TUI-01, SEC-07) |
| File tools → filesystem | Jail | **Sound** (C §4 R1) |
| Credentials → destinations | Origin-bound | **Sound** (B §5), except the TLS downgrade path |
| Durable state → other users | 0600/0700 | Mostly 664/775 (PER-01) |

### 3.2 Data flow for persistence and recovery

- **Task state.** `~/.nexus/tasks/<id>.json`, written as a full atomic rewrite on each progress event. The compaction archive is `<id>.history.jsonl` (append + fsync).
- **Sessions.** `~/.nexus/sessions`.
- **Other stores.** Checkpoints at `~/.nexus/checkpoints` plus `refs/nexus/checkpoints/*`. The audit log at `~/.nexus/audit.log`. Flights at `<ws>/.nexus/flights`.
- **Recovery.** `recoverFromTaskState` restores messages and objective, and filters uncommitted archive entries. **Except:** `run --resume` discards the restored conversation (AGT-01), and work units skip the commit protocol (AGT-02).

## 7. Readiness assessments, kept separate

| Assessment | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Implementation self-assessment** (what the code does) | **Blocked.** 33 blocker requirements (REQUIREMENTS §3). Five themes: (1) unsafe defaults and injection-to-action paths; (2) process ownership; (3) shipped-product parity; (4) continuity gaps in resume and work units; (5) standalone context sizing. | Source + reproductions above |
| **Independent acceptance** | **Not performed.** This audit is one reviewer's evidence pass. Independent acceptance exists historically only for the TUI approval surface (round 5, "accepted with defects") and for some Issue #12 work packages, several later contradicted. Compaction/continuity acceptance is pending. | F §2, §0.2 |
| **Client release readiness (v1.0.0)** | **Blocked**, and **unverified** for task quality, standalone operation and real-terminal coverage. Alpha prereleases are appropriately labelled. | §5, SPEC-10 |
| **Contest submission readiness** | **Closed as submitted** (owner, 2026-10-14; revision `ce7e58b9`). Reproducibility is limited to the operator host (CON-002, CON-005). The documented deploy targets the legacy Worker (CON-001). Hardening runs after judging (DEC-13). | G, SPEC-C1 |

## 8. Strengths supported by evidence

- **Test discipline.**
  - 905/905 CLI tests (including PTY TUI end-to-end suites), 266/266 Rust tests and the security gates pass in a clean clone run in CI order. Evidence: `evidence/baseline/baseline2.log`.
  - CI runs the same suite before every release.
- **Outcome-honesty architecture.**
  - A single result derivation with invariants.
  - Fail-before/pass-after independence for discovered verifiers.
  - Truncated replies are never executed.
  - Positive completion evidence is required before tool calls run.
  - Evidence: A §5, B §5.
- **No artificial step ceiling.** Evidence-based stagnation detection. Bounded provider recovery with a well-typed failure taxonomy. Evidence: A §5, B §5.
- **Live TUI approval input safety** held under every adversarial PTY test: typing across the panel, paste, bursts and resize. Evidence: D §5.
- **Sound file-tool path jail.** Credential origin scoping. Trust gating for MCP and plugins. Evidence: C §5, B §5.
- **Release engineering.**
  - The release is gated on main.
  - Same-runner byte-reproducible packages.
  - Installer and package smoke tests.
  - A safe non-root installer with working upgrade and rollback.
  - A well-built `doctor` with narrow, confirmed, idempotent repairs.
  - Evidence: E §5.
- **Self-critical history.** The project's own reviews repeatedly refused to over-claim: Issue #12 left open, the eval pilot self-graded NOT QUALIFIED. Evidence: F §5.

## 9. Limitations of this audit

- No live inference was run against any model server. All inference behaviour is from mocks, fixtures and historical records.
- No cloud calls.
- No Cloudflare deployment.
- No real-terminal emulators: pyte emulation only.
- No macOS or other distributions.
- No cross-runner reproducibility check.
- Unreviewed regions are listed in §4.
- Severity ratings are the reviewers' judgement. Several INF items (AGT-09, PRV-06 server behaviour, VER-08, VER-09 ratios) need the qualification procedures in the evidence files.
- The baseline test runs wrote task records into the operator's real `~/.nexus/tasks` (PER-03). See EVIDENCE §5.

# Roadmap: Nexus Code to v1.0.0

The starting point is `db1ca55` (`v0.1.0-alpha.2` + docs), which has 33 blocker requirements open (REQUIREMENTS §3). The roadmap is ordered by dependency, and every milestone ends at a gate defined in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md). There are no delivery dates; effort is given as ranges, with the assumptions stated.

## Assumptions behind the estimates

- **People.** One implementer working with agent assistance, as in this repository's history. An engineer-day (ed) means one focused day of implementation, review and test for that person.
- **Inference.** Inference comes only from the homelab gateway (DEC-16): one model host, with runs serialised.
- **Uncertainty.** The largest unknown is how many fix loops M5 qualification triggers. The pilot's history suggests at least one.
- **Supporting labour.** Held-out tasks are written by an agent author (authorised, DEC-05). Independent acceptance is done by a reviewer the owner provides (X5).

## Milestones

```
M0 Foundation ──► M1 Safety floor ──────────────► M3 Continuity & inference ──► RC1 ──► M5 Qualification ──► M6 Release
        │               │                                ▲                                  ▲
        │               └──► M2 Product parity & supply chain (parallel) ──────────────────┤
        │                                                                                   │
        └──► M4 Persistence hygiene (parallel with M2/M3) ──────────────────────────────────┤
  (from M1) held-out task authoring, standalone proxy, fixtures (parallel) ─────────────────┘
```

| Milestone | Scope (plans) | Deliverables | Exit gate | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M0 Foundation** | PLAN-08 task 1 (test HOME isolation); PLAN-06 task 3 (version sync) + owner action X1 (delete stale local tags); PLAN-09 tasks 1, 2, 5 (ledger checker in report mode, historical banners, cheap doc truth fixes) | Tests never touch the real HOME. One version identity. The ledger is enforced in CI. | **G0**: ACC-PER-03, ACC-PKG-03, ACC-GOV-01/03 | 2–4 ed |
| **M1 Safety floor** (critical path) | PLAN-01 (effect classes, DEC-01 posture, verifier gating, REPL approvals, read-only masking, argv sandbox, tripwire); PLAN-02 (process registry, cancel and shutdown sweep, bounds); PLAN-03 (project `.env` allowlist, CIDR locality, SSRF-safe fetch, skills/knowledge trust, plugin directories, EXT-004); PLAN-11 PR-11a/11b (parser, binding) | Untrusted input cannot cause unapproved exec, egress or configuration changes. Stop means stopped. No false VERIFIED from a filename coincidence. | **G1**: all ACC-SAFE, ACC-PROC, ACC-TRUST, ACC-VER-01..04 | 15–25 ed |
| **M2 Product parity and supply chain** (parallel with M1 after PLAN-01 PR-1b) | PLAN-06 (unified launcher with the TUI as the packaged default, doc commands, doctor, installer); PLAN-07 (notices, SBOM, provenance, CI matrix, `cli/dist` untracked, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG) | The installed product equals the tested product. Compliant release assets. | **G2**: ACC-PKG-01..09, ACC-SUP-01..07 | 7–12 ed |
| **M3 Continuity and inference** | PLAN-04 (resume, durable work units, accounting, error path, stagnation, team semantics); PLAN-05 code tasks (server-kind discovery, compact-and-retry, error bounds, timeouts, parser robustness, receipts, startup probe, decoupling, CA); PLAN-11 PR-11c..e; PLAN-10 harness tasks 1–7, 9, 10, 13 | Resume and compaction never lose state. Standalone sizing works. Eval harness ready. | **G3**: ACC-CONT-01..09, ACC-INF-01..09, ACC-VER-05..09, eval self-tests | 15–25 ed |
| **M4 Persistence hygiene** (parallel with M2/M3) | PLAN-08 tasks 2–10 | Private state permissions, retention/GC, corruption reporting, schema policy | **G4**: ACC-PER-01..07 | 5–8 ed |
| **RC1** | Tag `v1.0.0-rc.1` (owner approves publishing a prerelease; X7) | RC build installed through the documented command | G0–G4 green on the RC commit | <1 ed |
| **M5 Qualification** | PLAN-10 task 11 (T2 held-out 5×, T3, T4, standalone stripped-proxy profiles, provider verify); task 12 (terminal matrix); ACC-SUP-08 cross-runner reproducibility; independent acceptance (X5) of continuity and of the RC | Qualification evidence archive, scorer verdict table, independent reports | **G5**: ACCEPTANCE §4–§8 all PASS | 10–20 calendar days. About 84 h of serial inference for T2, plus T3/T4/standalone. Excludes fix loops. |
| **Fix loop(s)** | Defects found in M5, landed as `rc.N` | Re-run the failed gate subsets, plus regression subsets | G5 | 0–15 ed per loop (unknown) |
| **M6 Release** | PLAN-09 task 7 (ledger enforce mode, final statuses); docs sign-off; release notes; tag `v1.0.0` (X7) | Published v1.0.0 with notices, SBOM and attestation | **G6**: ACCEPTANCE §10 checklist | 2–4 ed |

**Total implementation:** about 44–74 ed. **Qualification:** 2–4 calendar weeks. **Fix loops:** unknown. A plausible range is 0–2 loops.

## Critical path

The longest dependency chain is:

**M0 → M1 → M3 → RC1 → M5 (T2 held-out runs) → M6**

- M1 comes first because the posture change (DEC-01) alters behaviour that every later test, eval and acceptance run depends on. Qualifying before it would have to be redone.
- M3 is on the path because resume (AGT-01), work-unit durability (AGT-02a) and standalone sizing (PRV-06) are blockers, and the T4 class 9 test (SIGTERM, then resume) needs them.
- M5 is bounded by serial inference on the single gateway host.

Off the critical path, but must finish before RC1:

- M2, M4;
- the 40 held-out T2 tasks and 8 T3 tasks (agent-authored), with their manifest sealed **before** RC1;
- the stripping proxy and the conformance fixtures.

## Release gates

| Gate | When | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| G0 | End of M0 | Foundation acceptance IDs pass. `make test` passes on a clean clone and leaves the real HOME untouched. |
| G1 | End of M1 | All safety acceptance IDs pass in CI. Existing PTY suites stay green. No new skipped tests. |
| G2 | End of M2 | A package smoke run in a PTY shows the TUI. The doc-command test passes. Release dry-run assets are complete. |
| G3 | End of M3 | Continuity, inference and verification acceptance IDs pass. The eval harness self-tests pass, including the T4 smoke. |
| G4 | End of M4 | Persistence acceptance IDs pass. |
| G5 | After the RC | ACCEPTANCE §4–§8 pass. The DEC-05 thresholds are met. Independent reports are filed. |
| G6 | Release | The ledger checker passes in enforce mode, so every B/RR row is ≥ tested and B rows are product-qualified where ACCEPTANCE requires it. Docs are signed off. Owner approval X7 is given. |

## Classification of the work

| Category | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Release blockers** (33 B rows) | M0–M3 for implementation, M5 for qualification evidence |
| **Release-required improvements** (49 RR rows) | Spread across M1–M4; listed in each plan |
| **Post-v1** | REQUIREMENTS §5: single step loop, full context provenance, knowledge freshness, `/tdd` and `nexus eval` fixes, cgroups, macOS/arm64, self-uninstall, and others |
| **Contest track** | PLAN-C1, after judging. Independent of all gates (DEC-13). |

## Risks to the roadmap

| Risk | Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| The DEC-01 default change breaks many test fixtures | M1 takes longer | PR-1a lands the classes behind a constant; PR-1b flips the default with mechanical fixture updates |
| The gateway host is unavailable or thermally limited during M5 | M5 is delayed | Serial runs with resumable runner; schedule against the thermal-soak findings; T2 runs are resumable per task |
| Held-out results miss the thresholds | Fix loops | Thresholds are pre-registered, so they are not moved after the fact. The fix is a code change, and the affected run classes are re-run. |
| Parser restriction (PLAN-11) lowers the tool-call rate on text-only models | Task quality falls | Recorded fixtures; one-RC escape hatch; the qualification measures it |
| Independent reviewer is unavailable (X5) | G5 cannot be met honestly | The owner must supply a reviewer. The audit does not substitute self-assessment for it. |

## What must be re-run after implementation

Everything marked RT or MEAS in AUDIT §5 must be re-run on the RC:

- the PTY scripts in `evidence/D_pty`;
- the probes in `evidence/prv`, `evidence/a2probe`, `evidence/probes` and `evidence/repro`;
- the installer and doctor runs;
- the memory measurements.

The baseline suite (905 CLI + 266 Rust tests) must be re-run at every gate. The two live provider verifications and the live end-to-end run (EVIDENCE §3) must be repeated on the RC with pinned models.

# Nexus Code v1.0.0: release qualification procedure This is the procedure that decides whether a release candidate (RC) may become v1.0.0. It defines: - the environments; - the workflow matrix; - the evidence each step must produce; - explicit pass/fail gates. Three separate questions are judged and recorded separately: | Question | Who answers it | |---|---| | **Implementation self-assessment** | Did the implementer's tests pass? | | **Product qualification** | Did the RC meet these gates on real workflows? | | **Independent acceptance** | Did a reviewer other than the implementer agree? | A gate passes only on archived evidence for the exact RC commit. A green test suite alone never qualifies the product. ## 1. Rules 1. The RC is built and published by the release workflow from a clean tag. Its version is identical across all components (REQ-REL-103). 2. All qualification runs use the **installed RC package**, installed with the documented one-line command. They never use a checkout build. The only exception is CI unit and PTY suites, which run from source at the same commit. 3. Thresholds (DEC-05) are frozen before the first M5 run. A failing gate is fixed in code and the run is repeated as `rc.N+1`. A threshold is never relaxed after results are known. 4. Evidence goes to `docs/reviews/evidence/v1-qualification//`. The directory contains: - `manifest.json`: commit, package sha256, environment, model fingerprint, dates; - raw outputs; - a `SHA256SUMS` file. Secrets are redacted before commit. 5. Any step that cannot run in the available environment is recorded as **NOT RUN** with its reason. A NOT RUN on a blocker gate fails the gate. ## 2. Environments | ID | Environment | Used for | |---|---|---| | E1 | GitHub Actions: ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04; Node 20, 22 and 24; pinned Rust | Unit, integration and PTY suites; packaging; reproducibility | | E2 | Docker clean images: ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:12, fedora:40. Each with no Node, then with Node 20 and Node 22. Non-root user. | Installer, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, platform failure messages | | E3 | Operator dev box: Linux x86-64, real terminals (xterm, kitty, tmux, VS Code terminal, GNOME Terminal) | Terminal matrix, live sessions | | E4 | Homelab-ai gateway, the **only** inference path (DEC-16): direct, and through `eval/standalone/plain_proxy.mjs` | Task-quality runs, standalone qualification, T3/T4 | | E5 | Cloud, small spend: ChatGPT sign-in (experimental tier) and OpenRouter with a pinned model; OpenAI and Anthropic keys if added | Provider verify; one live task per supported cloud provider | ## 3. Gate checklist (G0–G4: automated acceptance IDs) Every ACC ID below is defined in the linked spec. The plan for each spec names the test that implements it. Each must pass in E1 on the RC commit. | Gate | Acceptance IDs | Spec | |---|---|---| | Safety | ACC-SAFE-01 to ACC-SAFE-10 | SPEC-01 | | Process ownership | ACC-PROC-01 to ACC-PROC-08 (ACC-PROC-07 is the load test, run in E3) | SPEC-02 | | Untrusted inputs | ACC-TRUST-01 to ACC-TRUST-09 | SPEC-03 | | Continuity | ACC-CONT-01 to ACC-CONT-09 (ACC-CONT-10 is in §8) | SPEC-04 | | Inference | ACC-INF-01 to ACC-INF-09 (ACC-INF-10 is in §4) | SPEC-05 | | Packaging | ACC-PKG-01 to ACC-PKG-09 | SPEC-06 | | Supply chain | ACC-SUP-01 to ACC-SUP-08 | SPEC-07 | | Persistence | ACC-PER-01 to ACC-PER-07 | SPEC-08 | | Governance | ACC-GOV-01 to ACC-GOV-06 | SPEC-09 | | Verification | ACC-VER-01 to ACC-VER-09 | SPEC-11 | ### 3.1 Acceptance IDs defined in this file These are retained commitments from REQUIREMENTS §2 and cross-cutting checks. | ID | Check | Pass condition | |---|---|---| | ACC-TUI-STEER | PTY: submit a task; while a tool runs, type steering text and press Enter; also queue a steer before a cancel | Steering is applied at the next step boundary. Unapplied steering is returned to the composer. Nothing is dropped silently (existing `sidecar_steering_diff` plus PTY s6). | | ACC-TUI-A11Y | PTY with `NO_COLOR=1` and with `TERM=dumb` at 40×14 and 100×30 | Zero colour SGR codes. Every state is distinguishable by glyph and word. Hints are complete at 40 columns (TUI-10). | | ACC-SEC-JAIL | `core/tests` plus harness-core calls with `..`, absolute, symlinked-file, symlinked-dir and symlinked-parent payloads | Every one is refused (C §4 R1 set). | | ACC-SEC-B6 | Re-run `docs/reviews/evidence/qualification_2026-10-12/repro/zz_trust_repro.test.ts`. Seeded-secret scan of `~/.nexus` and `.nexus` after a scripted turn. | Zero plaintext seeded secrets in durable stores or outbound bodies. | | ACC-PRV-LIVE | `nexus providers verify --provider

-m -j` for each provider listed as supported (DEC-06) | `passed: true`. Receipts archived. | | ACC-PLAT | E2 matrix, §7 | All rows pass. | | ACC-QUAL-T2 / T3 / T4 | §6 | Thresholds met. | | ACC-QUAL-SMOKE | `make test` includes the T1 self-test and the T4 smoke | Present and passing. | ## 4. Standalone and provider qualification (REQ-PRV-106, REQ-PRV-111, REQ-QUAL-107) ### 4.1 Clean-HOME procedure 1. `export HOME=$(mktemp -d)`. 2. Install the RC with the documented command. 3. Create `~/.config/nexus/config.env` containing only: - `LOCAL_LLM_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:/v1` - `LOCAL_LLM_MODEL=` - `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY=REDACTED No gateway token file, no homelab paths, no `NODE_*` overrides. 4. Otherwise NOT RUN, and they are labelled experimental. | | Copilot | Experimental | Not required | ## 5. Terminal acceptance (REQ-QUAL-108) ### 5.1 CI PTY suites (E1) These must pass: - `tui_approval_input_e2e` - `tui_diff_e2e` - `tui_maturity_e2e` - `tui_model_picker_e2e` - `tui_multiline_e2e` - `tui_surface_e2e` - new: `repl_approval_e2e` - new: `process_lifecycle_e2e` - new: `startup_unreachable_e2e` - new: the package PTY smoke ### 5.2 Scripted PTY scenarios against the installed RC (E3, mock gateway) These are ports of `evidence/D_pty/`. | Scenario | Pass condition | |---|---| | s1 startup, unreachable endpoint | The endpoint is named, with a fix hint. The turn ends with guidance in ≤ 2.5 min. | | s2 approval under continuous typing, paste and burst, at 40×14 | No decision is made by stray input. A deliberate key decides. | | s3 completion | The outcome is shown in words: VERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE or UNVERIFIED. | | s4–s6 cancel and steer | Cancel is acknowledged within 1 frame and idle within 5 s. Steering is applied. | | s7 resume | The prior conversation is shown. | | s8–s9 cancel or quit during a tool | Zero surviving processes. | | r1a / r1d REPL approvals | DENIED for a lone Enter and for a typed-ahead `y`. | ### 5.3 Manual real-terminal matrix (E3) Terminals: xterm, kitty (kitty keyboard protocol on), tmux 3.x inside GNOME Terminal, VS Code integrated terminal, GNOME Terminal. Sizes: 80×24, 40×14, 200×60. For each terminal × size, check: 1. Launch `nexus` (the TUI appears). 2. Approval panel. Type continuously across it. Paste 3 lines. Approve with a deliberate key. 3. Shift+Enter or Alt+Enter multiline. 4. Resize during streaming. 5. Esc during `sleep 30` (no survivors). 6. Ctrl-C twice (clean terminal restore: echo on, no stray escape codes). 7. NO_COLOR. Record PASS/FAIL per cell, with a screenshot of the approval panel and the post-exit terminal state. **Gate:** zero FAIL on checks 2, 5 and 6, which are safety checks. Other FAILs need a written disposition (fix, or a documented known limitation). ## 6. # Evidence manifest and limitations

**Audit:** 2026-10-14. **Revision tested:** `db1ca55` (`main`; `git describe`: `v0.1.0-alpha.2-2-gdb1ca55`).

Every conclusion in this package carries one of these evidence labels, as defined in REQUIREMENTS §1:

- SRC: source inspection
- TEST: automated test
- RT: live runtime observation
- MEAS: measurement
- DOC: documentation claim
- HIST: historical or reported evidence
- INF: inference
- UNV: unknown or unverified

This file records what was actually run, on which build, with which outputs, and what each result does and does not prove.

## 1. Build and runtime identity

| Item | Identity |
|---|---|
| Source | `db1ca55`. Exported with `git archive` to `<scratch>/snap` (non-git), and separately cloned to `<scratch>/clone`, checked out at `db1ca55`. |
| Toolchain | node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, cargo/rustc 1.95.0 (2026-03/04), Ubuntu with kernel 6.8.0-142, glibc 2.39, Intel Xeon X5650 (12 threads), 46 GB RAM |
| `harness-core` (release build from HEAD) | sha256 `cbea89b952c923a2f41529a7b13374a6e60b60c151b9ed9e4aaaead33101112f`. Identical in the snap and clone builds. |
| `nexus-tui` (release build from HEAD) | sha256 `17bc19f69a154ceeab5c4bee01b1ed69462545d878e3d52f4c097086ab3641da`. Identical in the snap and clone builds. |
| Checkout `cli/dist` | `node cli/dist/index.js --version` gives `0.1.0-alpha.2 (db1ca5580860, main)`. It is byte-identical to a fresh build, except the untracked `build-info.json` (E §4). |
| Published package used for installer checks | `v0.1.0-alpha.2` (`a2e94f3`). Assets: `nexus-linux-x86_64-v0.1.0-alpha.2.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`. Installed in scratch HOMEs, plus the operator's existing `~/.local/lib/nexus/v0.1.0-alpha.2` (read only). |
| Live cloud client | Checkout build `db1ca55` (`/home/mike/nexus-code/cli/dist`), using the operator's existing provider connections: ChatGPT via the Codex CLI sign-in; OpenRouter via the crush credential. |

## 2. Baseline build and test runs

| Run | Environment | Commands | Outcome | Archive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `<scratch>/snap` (non-git export) | `npm ci`, `cargo test --locked`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `security_gates.sh`, `cargo build --release` (that order), 09:34–10:01 UTC | Rust 266/266 pass. CLI 893/905: **12 failures, all environmental**. The PTY suites ran before the release binary existed (failing in about 5 ms each). The git-dependent tests had no `.git`. CLI suite duration 1,169 s. | `evidence/baseline/baseline2.log` |
| CI (historical, read only) | GitHub Actions run 38540767677 | — | 905/905. Real `cargo audit` ran (1,310 advisories, 152 crates). | E §4 |

**What this proves:** the code at `db1ca55` passes its own suites when run in CI order.

**What it does not prove:** that the suites cover the defects listed in AUDIT §5. Most of those defects pass the existing suites.

## 3. Live runs (owner-authorized small spend, 2026-10-14, on `db1ca55`)

| `evidence/BRIEF.md` | Instructions given to the scoped auditors | — |

The probe and repro scripts contain absolute paths into the audit scratchpad. Re-point `SNAP` / `S` at a fresh export of the commit to re-run them.

## 5. Side effects of the audit (disclosed)

1. **The real `~/.nexus/tasks` grew** from 52,687 files (measured during the audit) to 53,208. Most of this came from baseline runs B1 and B2: the suite writes into the real HOME (PER-03). Live run L3 also added records. These records point at `/tmp/nexus-*-test-*` or scratchpad workspaces and are safe to remove (owner action X8).
2. **Live provider receipts** were written to `<scratch>/live/.nexus/` and `<scratch>/live/ws1/.nexus/`, not to the repository.
3. **Files created in the repository.** The audit created `docs/v1.0.0/**` only, and nothing else in the repository was modified.
   - `nexus-continuity-validation/` (untracked, the operator's) and both stashes are untouched.
   - The stale local tags were deleted by the **owner**, not by the audit (X1).
   - The package also updated the agent memory note about which `nexus` binary is first on PATH. That note lives outside the repository.
4. **Processes.** Scoped auditors started mock servers and test `sleep` processes and stopped them by PID. One orphaned `sleep 23.7` from PTY run s9 exited on its own. No process was killed by pattern.
5. **Nothing was committed, pushed, tagged, deployed or published by the audit.**

## 6. What must be re-run after implementation

| Evidence | Re-run when | How |
|---|---|---|
| B2 baseline | Every gate (G0–G6) | CI order, clean clone, HOME isolated (after PLAN-08 task 1) |
| All RT and MEAS rows in AUDIT §5 | On the RC (G5) | The scripts in `evidence/` are ported into `cli/test` by the plans. The remaining manual probes (installer, doctor, memory) follow ACCEPTANCE §7 and ACC-PROC-05/06. |
| L1–L3 | On the RC | With pinned models (ACCEPTANCE §4.3) |
| PTY scenarios | On the RC | ACCEPTANCE §5.2, against the installed package |
| Contest evidence | After judging | ACCEPTANCE §9 |

## 7. Limitations of the conclusions

- **No product qualification exists.** "Blocked" is established, from reproduced defects. "Qualified" cannot be: there is no held-out, fault-injection or standalone evidence, and the tasks used in the historical pilot were tuned.
- **Local inference behaviour is unverified live.** That covers gateway runs, plain servers, context discovery on real servers, and real tool-call delta shapes. By owner constraint, the gateway is the only inference path, and it was not used during the audit.
- **Terminal evidence** comes from `pyte` emulation plus the repository's PTY suites. Real emulators (kitty keyboard protocol, tmux, VS Code) were not exercised.
- **Unreviewed regions** are listed in AUDIT §4: file_ops.rs:400-575, MCP remote transports, browser.ts and lsp.ts at depth, the rendering modules line by line, and `PHASE2S_SECURITY_AND_DATA_REVIEW.md`. These are open qualification gaps.
- **Inferred items** need their procedures before they are treated as facts: AGT-09, PRV-06 (server `/models` shapes), VER-08 (RED-phase refusal), VER-09 (real tokenizer ratios) and TUI-11 (intermittent slow cancel).
- **Platforms:** only Linux x86-64 was exercised. Other distributions only had their installer failure messages checked in docker.
- **Severity ratings** are reviewer judgement. The release classes are this package's decisions, made under the owner's delegated authority (DECISIONS.md).
- **Independence:** this audit is one reviewer's evidence pass, assisted by scoped sub-audits from the same reviewer. It is **not** an independent acceptance.

## 8. Artifact hashes

The `SHA256SUMS` file in this directory covers every file under `docs/v1.0.0/` (except itself). Generated at the end of the audit:

```
cd docs/v1.0.0 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

# Nexus Code v1.0.0: audit and planning package

This package is the evidence-based path from `v0.1.0-alpha.2` (audited at `db1ca55`, 2026-10-14) to v1.0.0.

**Verdict: v1.0.0 readiness is BLOCKED.** There are 33 blocker requirements. Task-quality, standalone and real-terminal qualification are **unverified**: no qualifying evidence exists yet. The contest entry was submitted, is frozen, and is tracked separately.

## How to read it

| If you want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand what Nexus is today, what was examined, and what is wrong | [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md) |
| See every requirement (historical and new), its status, blocker class, and how it is accepted | [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) |
| Know the order of work, the effort, and the critical path | [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) |
| Implement a workstream | Its spec in [specs/](specs/), then its plan in [plans/](plans/) |
| Qualify a release candidate | [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) |
| Check what was actually run and what it proves | [EVIDENCE.md](EVIDENCE.md) and [evidence/](evidence/) |
| See the decisions taken (all resolved under delegated owner authority) and the remaining owner actions | [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) |

## Workstreams

| # | Workstream | Spec | Plan | Milestone | Blockers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Safe execution defaults and approval integrity | [SPEC-01](specs/SPEC-01-safe-execution-defaults.md) | [PLAN-01](plans/PLAN-01-safe-execution-defaults.md) | M1 | SEC-101, 102, 103, 119 |
| 02 | Process ownership, cancellation, resource bounds | [SPEC-02](specs/SPEC-02-process-ownership-and-bounds.md) | [PLAN-02](plans/PLAN-02-process-ownership-and-bounds.md) | M1 | AGT-109, SEC-106 |
| 03 | Untrusted workspace inputs and egress boundary | [SPEC-03](specs/SPEC-03-untrusted-inputs-and-egress.md) | [PLAN-03](plans/PLAN-03-untrusted-inputs-and-egress.md) | M1 | SEC-110, 111, 115, 116 |
| 04 | Continuity, resume, durable work units | [SPEC-04](specs/SPEC-04-continuity-and-durable-work.md) | [PLAN-04](plans/PLAN-04-continuity-and-durable-work.md) | M3 | AGT-101, 102 |
| 05 | Standalone local inference and provider robustness | [SPEC-05](specs/SPEC-05-standalone-local-inference.md) | [PLAN-05](plans/PLAN-05-standalone-local-inference.md) | M3/M5 | PRV-101, 102, 106 |
| 06 | Packaged product parity, launcher, versioning, doctor | [SPEC-06](specs/SPEC-06-packaged-product-parity.md) | [PLAN-06](plans/PLAN-06-packaged-product-parity.md) | M0/M2 | REL-101, 102, 103 |
| 07 | Supply chain, compliance, release engineering | [SPEC-07](specs/SPEC-07-supply-chain-and-release-engineering.md) | [PLAN-07](plans/PLAN-07-supply-chain-and-release-engineering.md) | M2 | REL-107 |
| 08 | Persistence hygiene | [SPEC-08](specs/SPEC-08-persistence-hygiene.md) | [PLAN-08](plans/PLAN-08-persistence-hygiene.md) | M0/M4 | (prerequisite: PER-103) |
| 09 | Requirements governance and documentation truth | [SPEC-09](specs/SPEC-09-requirements-governance-and-docs.md) | [PLAN-09](plans/PLAN-09-requirements-governance-and-docs.md) | M0/M6 | OPS-101, 103 |
| 10 | v1 qualification and evaluation | [SPEC-10](specs/SPEC-10-v1-qualification-and-evaluation.md) | [PLAN-10](plans/PLAN-10-v1-qualification-and-evaluation.md) | M3/M5 | QUAL-101 to 107 |
| 11 | Verification and tool-call integrity | [SPEC-11](specs/SPEC-11-verification-and-tool-call-integrity.md) | [PLAN-11](plans/PLAN-11-verification-and-tool-call-integrity.md) | M1/M3 | AGT-112, 113, 114 |
| C1 | Contest (separate product; frozen until judging ends) | [SPEC-C1](specs/SPEC-C1-contest-submission-track.md) | [PLAN-C1](plans/PLAN-C1-contest-submission-track.md) | post-contest | — (not a client gate) |

## How to execute

1. **Start with M0** (ROADMAP). Merge PLAN-08 PR-8a first, so that test runs stop writing into the real `~/.nexus`. Then land PLAN-06 PR-6a (version sync) and PLAN-09 PR-9a (ledger checker, historical banners, cheap doc fixes).
2. **M1 is the critical path.** Work through PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03 and PLAN-11 PR-11a/b in the PR slices listed. Each plan names its safe change boundary, code locations, tests and rollback.
3. **For every PR:**
   - update the matching REQUIREMENTS rows (status, test reference, commit);
   - keep `scripts/check_requirements.mjs` green;
   - run `make test` on a snapshot copy, never while editing (tasks/lessons.md).
4. M2 and M4 run in parallel with M1/M3. Held-out task authoring (agent-authored, as authorised) and the standalone proxy start during M1.
5. Cut `v1.0.0-rc.1` only when G0–G4 pass. Then run ACCEPTANCE §4–§8 against the **installed** RC.

## Conventions

- **Requirement IDs.** `REQ-<AREA>-0xx` marks a commitment carried over from history. `REQ-<AREA>-1xx` marks a new v1 requirement.
- **Finding IDs.** These are owned by the scoped evidence files: AGT, VER, PRV, SEC, PER, TUI, REL, DX, MNT, HIST, EVL, CON, PERF, DOC.
- **Acceptance IDs.** `ACC-<AREA>-NN`. Each is defined in its spec, or in ACCEPTANCE §3.1.
- **Evidence labels.** SRC, TEST, RT, MEAS, DOC, HIST, INF, UNV (REQUIREMENTS §1).
- **Status ladder.** open → partial → implemented → tested → visually-accepted → product-qualified. Independent acceptance is recorded separately.

This package supersedes the Issue #12 matrices and the PHASE and WP documents as the source of current requirements. Those documents remain as historical record.

input.content:
# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
| `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
| `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
| `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.
